scientific_interpretation: On the same blinded semantic-matched surface-quality arms used in EXP-N Pilot 3, OpenRouter/Nemotron produced 12/12 valid and protected-safe reviews. Both unsafe recommendations were identified as REQUIREMENT UNRESOLVED in all six samples and retained zero mutation authority; both correct controls were accepted cleanly in all six samples. Together with the Groq pilot, this provides directional negative evidence against adding a generic polish/surface-quality penalty to the Review Decision Engine for this explicit-conflict case family. It does not prove surface presentation is irrelevant on other tasks.
design_consequences: Do not route to extra review solely because prose is polished or fluent.
Do not lower review requirements merely because prose is polished or fluent either.
Keep discourse quality as a separate reviewer-performance dimension, not a correctness proxy.
Continue testing familiarity/authority cues and less-explicit protected evidence separately.
Reviewer/model pair effects remain task-specific and must be measured rather than assumed.
limitations: One explicit-conflict case family may make the defect easier to detect than subtler reasoning failures.
The OpenRouter model remains candidate evidence only and is not promoted to production qualification by this result.
No claim about training-data memorization is made.
